articles.title: County Championship cricket: Craig Overton, Jack Leach help Somerset remain top with crushing win at Leicestershire
articles.summary: After title rivals Warwickshire claimed victory inside two days against Glamorgan, leaders Somerset responded with aplomb against Leicestershire to clinch 377-run victory and return top of the Rothesay County Championship as Craig Overton and Jack Leach stood out
articles.body:
After title rivals Warwickshire claimed victory inside two days against Glamorgan, leaders Somerset responded with aplomb.

Henry Nicholls' unbeaten 100 helped the visitors declare on 316-5 to set Leicestershire an insurmountable victory target of 523.

The real question was whether Somerset could wrap up this latest triumph with a day to spare and Leicestershire only managed to bat out 45.1 overs, with Overton the pick of the bowlers - 4-33 - and England's forgotten man Leach taking 3-30 to dismiss the hosts for 145.

Nottinghamshire , who are also in the title picture, responded to being dismissed for 104 at Trent Bridge on day three to fight back and take control against Hampshire .

During a 19-wicket day, Hampshire were dismissed for 304 before England's teenage prospect Manny Lumsden ripped through Nottinghamshire's top order in sensational fashion.

After Haseeb Hameed had watched Nottinghamshire collapse to set only 178 for victory, Olly Stone and Dillon Pennington ran amok to reduce Hampshire to 61-6 at stumps and set up a tantalising final day, with England U19 international Ben Mayes on 21 not out.

Essex 's relegation fears increased after they suffered defeat by an innings and 106 runs at Yorkshire .

After Essex were all out for 171 - despite an unbeaten fifty by debutant George Bell - they followed on and were rolled for 113, with home bowler Kuldeep Yadav able to claim match figures of 10-120.

Ben Foakes made 54 to help Surrey to 294-7 against Sussex before bad light in Hove ensured they will trail by 99 runs ahead of Friday's final day.

In Division Two, Northamptonshire piled the pressure on promotion rivals Kent after they won by six wickets at Worcestershire , who were all out for 182 in their second innings, and George Bartlett's unbeaten 19 got his team over the line in pursuit of 94 at New Road.

Kent have dropped to third but will return to second if they can bat out day four at Derbyshire or chase down an unlikely total of 434. After the hosts declared on 352-8, visiting openers Zak Crawley and Ben Compton survived nine balls before the close.

Leaders Durham are in control after Middlesex were reduced to 55-2 in pursuit of 424.

Rocky Flintoff made a first-class best 57 not out, but Lancashire are 120-6 with 128 runs required for victory over Gloucestershire .

articles.title: Joe Root's struggles and England century drought against Pakistan the only concerns from improved post-Bazball batting, says Nasser Hussain
articles.summary: England in complete control of third Test against Pakistan with tourists 268 runs behind at stumps; England dominate day two with the bat but Nasser Hussain highlights two areas for improvement
articles.body:
England piled on 453 runs to establish a commanding first-innings lead of 320 in the third Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston.

The hosts were firmly in control and on course for a 3-0 series sweep, with Pakistan closing on 52-2, still 268 runs adrift, when rain curtailed play.

"I've liked the tempo of the batting in this series," former England captain Hussain said.

"We talked about it earlier in the Bazball era, England going too hard and not seizing opportunities.

"They've got the tempo right, especially through the middle order with Harry Brook, Jamie Smith, Dan Lawrence and Gus Atkinson.

"I know it's a poor Pakistan bowling attack, but even Josh Tongue and Jofra Archer have contributed with the bat.

"I like Emilio Gay's tempo at the top of the order. He bats time and knows when to absorb pressure. English cricket, and this side in particular, have been crying out for that."

Despite the overwhelming positives, Hussain highlighted two areas England have yet to address during the Pakistan series.

Root's four dismissals have all been lbw, with the world's second-highest Test run-scorer continuing to wrestle with that mode of dismissal.

"Obviously, there are two boxes they haven't ticked," Hussain explained.

"Their greatest player is struggling with one specific type of dismissal: lbw.

"It's so obvious he's struggling. He tried to address it in the first innings, made a technical adjustment and then got out lbw again."

'England need to convert starts to big scores'

Meanwhile, England's wait for a hundred has reached historic levels.

Brook (75), Smith (69), Lawrence (65), Gay (60) and Ollie Robinson (50) have all reached fifty without kicking on to three figures.

A total of 14 half-centuries have been scored across the series without a single hundred, the first time that has happened in a Test series in England since the 1888 Ashes.

"The other one is getting hundreds," Hussain added.

"You can beat Pakistan with 40s, 50s and 60s. To beat Australia, or the New Zealand side we saw earlier in the summer, you need big hundreds and massive scores

"England just need to convert those starts into big scores."

Reflecting on the absence of a century in the Test series, former England bowler Stuart Broad has called for a reassessment of what constitutes a good score after a scorching summer has made conditions favourable for bowlers.

Broad argued that some scores this summer have been every bit as valuable as centuries on flatter pitches.

"Top-order batting has been very difficult in this series," Broad said.

"Root, England's best-ever player, has struggled for runs in this series. If he's struggling, it's OK for everyone else to struggle.

"We can't praise the likes of Ollie Robinson, who is getting 20-odd wickets at an average of around 6.00, and also say, 'We should be getting more centuries.'

"To be honest, this summer I think a 60 has felt like a hundred.

"You've had to work as hard for a 60 on these pitches as you would for a hundred on a normal Test match surface."

articles.title: 'No, not really': Marcus Trescothick unsure of future with England Test side
articles.summary: Cricket News: Marcus Trescothick is not sure if he will continue with England's Test team after Stephen Fleming takes charge as the permanent head coach.Trescothick.
articles.body: Marcus Trescothick is not sure if he will continue with England's Test team after Stephen Fleming takes charge as the permanent head coach.Trescothick was the interim head coach during England's recent 3-0 home series win over Pakistan. He took charge after Brendon McCullum left the Test coaching role, with Fleming set to take over ahead of the winter series against South Africa.Trescothick had worked as McCullum's assistant coach and is now waiting to find out whether he will remain part of the Test coaching staff under Fleming.Trescothick unsure about Test roleWhen asked if he knew what his Test role would be once Fleming takes over, Trescothick admitted that there was no clear answer yet."No, not really," Trescothick said when asked whether he had an idea of his Test role in the future, as quoted by Cricinfo. "I've spoken with Rob Key a little bit over the last couple of weeks and had bits of discussions on what might happen."I think when Stephen’s (Fleming) over and then they - Rob and Stephen and Brendon - can get together and really sort of thrash out exactly how it's going to look, then we'll probably be involved in those sort of conversations afterwards."Trescothick joins England's white-ball setupTrescothick will now travel to Southampton to join McCullum and the England white-ball team for the Sri Lanka T20I series. He will be joined by fellow assistants Sarah Taylor, Tim Southee and Jeetan Patel. Kevin Pietersen will also join the group as a specialist mentor."Our immediate plan is obviously then looking at the Sri Lanka series we're now straight into, with the possibility of going maybe into Pakistan. But I think within the next couple of weeks we'll know a bit more."I love doing both formats. It's been brilliant and (I'm) privileged to be in the position of being assistant coach where you're on the road because it's great fun and you're with the team and you're working with the best. There's nothing better than working with your own national country, of course. But we'll see. We'll see how it pans out."Joe Root praises TrescothickEngland Test captain Joe Root praised Trescothick for the way he handled the team during the Pakistan series."I think the way that he's worked with me, the way that he's worked with the group, has been outstanding," Root said. "And I hope he takes a lot of confidence from it and if he ever gets the opportunity to be a head coach further down the line, it's been great for him and he's done a brilliant job over the course of the three games."Trescothick wants England voice in Test setupTrescothick also stressed the importance of having people in the Test coaching staff who understand the specific needs of English players and the England team."As much as we can within the course of coaching systems, you want someone within that that can highlight things that are important with England players and England teams and England series that you play," said Trescothick. "Because they are different to other countries and unique in their own way."We want to try and promote our own from within and get them up to the top because there's nothing better, I don't think, than if you can get to that point. It's not the be all and end all. But, I think, as much as we can have the representation in there, then the better it'll be."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Why is Vaibhav Sooryavanshi not playing vs Afghanistan in 1st T20I?
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India made a big selection call for the first T20I against Afghanistan at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi on Sunday, with Sanju Samson ge.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India made a big selection call for the first T20I against Afghanistan at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi on Sunday, with Sanju Samson getting the nod over young batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.Captain Shreyas Iyer won the toss and decided to bowl first. India also brought Jasprit Bumrah back into the playing XI and picked specialist spinner Varun Chakaravarthy ahead of Yash Thakur.Why is Vaibhav Sooryavanshi not playing?India chose experience in the opening game, with Samson selected in the XI instead of Vaibhav.Iyer also confirmed that Washington Sundar and two other players were left out, making it clear that team combination was behind the decision."It's a luxury to have him (Bumrah) in the squad -- he carries lot of great attitude when it comes to winning matches. Vaibhav (Sooryavanshi) is not playing, neither are Washington and two more."Iyer later explained that managing the team combination was difficult."That is more difficult, I feel, but I would say if Vaibhav (Sooryavanshi) is not playing, then Washington (Sundar) is not playing and there are two more which you'll get to know".Samson was named as India's wicketkeeper, with Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan, Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma also in the batting group.India also picked Nitish Kumar Reddy, Shivam Dube and Axar Patel before going with Arshdeep Singh, Bumrah and Varun Chakaravarthy as the bowling options.Iyer said India had played several matches in Delhi and wanted to make use of the conditions by bowling first."We’re going to bowl first. I mean, when you have played in Delhi, you know what the pitch has got to offer and we’ve played quite a bit of matches over here. So based on that and looking at the conditions, that’s really both. [On his first ten matches as India captain]It's been a roller coaster ride, but if you see the previous series which we played against Zimbabwe, there were a lot of positives and the boys were optimistic in their approach. So, that's the attitude we've got to carry in this series as well."Jasprit Bumrah returnsBumrah returned to the India XI after missing recent assignments following the left-knee injury that ruled him out of an ODI in England and two Tests in Sri Lanka.Iyer called having Bumrah in the squad a "luxury" and highlighted his experience and ability to win matches."[On having Jasprit Bumrah available in the squad] Yes, certainly. I think it's a luxury to have him in the squad because he's immensely experienced and he carries a lot of great attitude when it comes to winning matches. So, we know he's a match winner and we know what he's got to offer."Afghanistan make changesAfghanistan captain Ibrahim Zadran said his team would have bowled first had they won the toss."We would have bowled first. Unfortunately, we lost the toss and we will think about batting. We will try to put a good total on the board."Zadran said Afghanistan were excited to host India and asked fans to support both teams."Yeah, it's a great feeling for us. It is a pleasure to host India, here in India for the first time. We are trying to enjoy ourselves, trying to have a good series against them."He added: "We have got lots of support from the fans in the past as well, and just requesting them to come support, both teams. I hope they don't forget us, but hopefully they come and support their own player, their own team, and give their energy to the players."Afghanistan also made changes to their side."Naveen(-ul-Haq) is not playing, Noor Ahmad, and Abdullah (Ahmadzai) and Naveen-ul-Haq, he's not match ready for today. Yeah, we will think about him for the second and third game," Afghanistan captain Ibrahim Zadran said.India vs Afghanistan 1st T20I: Playing XIsAfghanistan: Ibrahim Zadran (c), Rahmanullah Gurbaz (wk), Sediqullah Atal, Darwish Rasooli, Azmatullah Omarzai, Gulbadin Naib, Mohammad Nabi, Rashid Khan, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Noor Ahmad, Fazalhaq FarooqiIndia: Sanju Samson (wk), Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan, Shreyas Iyer (c), Tilak Varma, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Shivam Dube, Axar Patel, Arshdeep Singh, Jasprit Bumrah, Varun ChakaravarthyGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: India captain Harmanpreet Kaur won the toss and elected to bat first against Sri Lanka in the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday.India have made their first change of the tournament, bringing Gunalan Kamalini into the playing XI in place of Pratika Rawal. Kamalini gets her first opportunity in this edition of the Asia Cup and will play only her second T20I for India.The change comes after India fielded an unchanged XI in their opening four matches.India aim for record eighth Asia Cup titleBoth India and Sri Lanka have remained unbeaten on their way to the final, although India have looked the more dominant side throughout the tournament. The Women in Blue have produced strong performances across batting, bowling and fielding, with Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma leading the run-scoring charts for India.With the ball, Deepti Sharma and Shree Charani have been among India's standout performers, claiming 11 and eight wickets respectively. India are chasing a record-extending eighth Asia Cup title, having previously won four editions in the ODI format and three in T20Is.Sri Lanka rely on Athapaththu and DilhariSri Lanka have also reached the final unbeaten but have not been as consistent with the bat. articles.title: After IND vs AFG first, ‘Vande Mataram’ set to become regular before India matches
articles.summary: Cricket News: New Delhi: For the first time ever, the national song, 'Vande Mataram', was sung before the match between India and Afghanistan at the Arun Jaitley St.
articles.body: New Delhi: For the first time ever, the national song, 'Vande Mataram', was sung before the match between India and Afghanistan at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi on Sunday. The national song was followed by the standard practice of national anthems of both countries.It must be mentioned here that 'Vande Mataram' was sung during the Delhi Premier League final also, which also took place at the same venue. Curiously, it was not played during other state leagues in Odisha and Punjab.It has been learnt that it is going to be a practice going forward in matches involving the Indian team in India. "This is going to be followed in all events in India going forward. It is going to be a practice and it is not just about this stadium," said a source.It comes on the heels of Parliament passing a bill that made any insult to the national song a punishable offence. The full official version of ‘Vande Mataram’ comprises six stanzas - which was sung before the first of the three match series.As the 150th anniversary of 'Vande Mataram' was celebrated, the Home Ministry had directed that all six stanzas must be sung when 'Jana Gana Mana' is also sung."The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026 amends Section 3 of the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971. It extends the same legal protection to the National Song, Vande Mataram that is currently afforded to the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana. The amendment makes it an offence to intentionally prevent the singing of the National Song or to cause a disturbance to an assembly engaged in its singing," said a PIB statement in July.Prior to the teams taking the field for the national song and anthems, India skipper Shreyas Iyer had won the toss and chosen to field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Cricket News: Arshdeep Singh produced the standout bowling performance for India, taking 3/19 as India restricted Afghanistan to 156/8 in the opening game of the th.
articles.body: Arshdeep Singh produced the standout bowling performance for India, taking 3/19 as India restricted Afghanistan to 156/8 in the opening game of the three-match T20I series on Sunday.However, Arshdeep also bowled 51 wides, the most by any bowler for a team since January 2025.Arshdeep's 51 wides accounted for 7.4% of all the balls he bowled during the period. Renegades' R Ngarava and West Indies' Jason Holder follow with 38 wides each, while New Zealand's Jacob Duffy and West Indies' Romario Shepherd have bowled 36 each.Arshdeep strikes at crucial momentsJasprit Bumrah bowled some sharp deliveries, but Arshdeep stole the show with his 3/19 as India kept Afghanistan under pressure for most of the innings.The two spinners, Varun Chakravarthy (1/16 in 4 overs) and Axar Patel (1/27 in 4 overs), controlled the game during the first 10 overs.Bumrah (1/26 in 4 overs) also bowled at full tilt and sent down 16 dot balls. He removed former Kolkata Knight Riders batter Rahmanullah Gurbaz for a duck after the ball kicked up and Gurbaz edged it to Abhishek Sharma, who took a smart low catch at first slip.Arshdeep used variations and changes of pace to make breakthroughs at important moments.Most wides bowled since Jan 2025 (FM team)51 Arshdeep Singh (7.4% of all balls)38 R Ngarava (5.8%)/ J Holder (5.2%)36 J Duffy (5.8%)/ R Shepherd (8.6%)Arshdeep removes Nabi, Rashid strugglesIbrahim Zadran (13) and Sediqullah Atal (11) hit a few shots before a mix-up ended the Afghanistan captain's innings.Arshdeep then bowled a wide yorker that Atal tried to dig out. Bumrah, standing at fly slip, took an easy catch.Gulbadin Naib (2) played an inside-out shot against Axar Patel and was caught by Nitish Reddy. Varun then continued to attack the stumps and breached Darwish Rasooli's defence, leaving Afghanistan at 43/5 in seven overs.But Azmatullah Omarzai counter-attacked and targeted Nitish Reddy, who became the weak link in India's attack.Arshdeep returned for his second spell and clean bowled the dangerous Mohammad Nabi after being hit for a six.Once Nabi was dismissed, Afghanistan suffered another mini-collapse. articles.title: Abhishek Sharma’s 22-ball fifty, Arshdeep’s three-for lead India to seven-wicket win over Afghanistan in 1st T20I
articles.summary: Cricket News: Abhishek Sharma produced a breathtaking batting display as India began their three-match T20I series against Afghanistan with a commanding seven-wicke.
articles.body: Abhishek Sharma produced a breathtaking batting display as India began their three-match T20I series against Afghanistan with a commanding seven-wicket victory at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi.Chasing 157, India raced to 157/3 in just 13.4 overs, with Abhishek smashing 82 off only 32 balls to take the game away from Afghanistan. His innings featured seven fours and seven sixes, while Ishan Kishan provided valuable support with a composed 42.Afghanistan stumble before Omarzai-Nabi rescue actAfter being asked to bat, Afghanistan endured a dramatic collapse at the top. India's pace attack struck early, with Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh and the supporting bowlers putting the visitors under pressure. Afghanistan slipped to 43/5, leaving their innings in serious danger of folding for a modest total.However, Azmatullah Omarzai and Mohammad Nabi launched a counterattack to revive Afghanistan's innings. The pair added 83 runs, taking the visitors past 150 and giving their bowlers something to defend.Omarzai finished unbeaten on 64 off 44 balls, while Nabi contributed 33 as Afghanistan eventually posted 156/8.India's bowlers had Afghanistan in trouble for much of the innings. Arshdeep Singh was the pick of the attack, finishing with 3/19, while Bumrah also made an impact on his return to the T20I side. Axar Patel and Varun Chakravarthy chipped in with a wicket apiece. The disciplined bowling effort meant India needed only 157 to take the lead in the series.Abhishek Sharma turns chase into a one-sided affairIndia's chase suffered an early setback when Sanju Samson was dismissed for 10, but Afghanistan's hopes of defending the total disappeared almost immediately. Abhishek Sharma launched a spectacular counterattack, reaching his half-century in just 22 balls.The left-hander continued to take on the Afghanistan attack, eventually smashing 82 from 32 deliveries at a strike rate of 256. His seven sixes and seven fours turned what could have been a tricky chase into a procession.While Abhishek supplied the fireworks, Ishan Kishan played the ideal supporting role. Kishan scored 42 off 33 balls, helping India build a commanding partnership and maintain a huge asking-rate advantage. Abhishek eventually fell short of a century, but by then India were already within touching distance of victory.Captain Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma completed the chase, with India reaching 157/3 in only 13.4 overs.India take 1-0 leadIndia's seven-wicket victory came with 38 balls to spare, giving them a 1-0 lead in the three-match series. The second T20I will be played in Delhi on September 15, before the series concludes on September 17.Brief Scores: Afghanistan: 156/8 (Azmatullah Omarzai 64*, Mohammed Nabi 33, Arshdeep Singh 3/19) beat India: 157/3 in 13.4 overs (Abhishek Sharma 82, Ishan Kishan 42, Mohammad Nabi 2/28).Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Harmanpreet's India avenge 2024 final defeat, beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs to lift eighth Women's Asia Cup title
articles.summary: Cricket News: India Women are back on top of Asia. Harmanpreet Kaur’s side produced a commanding all-round performance to beat Sri Lanka Women by 72 runs in the Wom.
articles.body: India Women are back on top of Asia. Harmanpreet Kaur’s side produced a commanding all-round performance to beat Sri Lanka Women by 72 runs in the Women’s T20 Asia Cup 2026 final at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, reclaiming the continental crown and avenging their defeat in the 2024 final.After opting to bat first, India posted an imposing 183/5 in 20 overs, powered by a sensational opening partnership between Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana. The Indian bowlers then completed the job in emphatic fashion, bowling Sri Lanka out for 111 to seal a comprehensive victory.The victory gives India a record-extending eighth Women's Asia Cup title and underlines their dominance in the continental tournament.Shafali, Smriti set up India’s commanding totalIndia’s innings was built around a devastating opening stand between Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana.Shafali smashed 68 off just 39 balls, striking nine fours and two sixes, while Mandhana contributed a fluent 59 off 39 deliveries. Together, they added 129 runs for the opening wicket, putting Sri Lanka under immense pressure from the outset.Their aggressive batting gave India the perfect platform before Sri Lanka’s bowlers fought back with wickets in the middle overs. Gunalan Kamalini, however, provided the finishing touch with a quick-fire 15 not out from just five balls, including a huge six on the final delivery, taking India to 183/5.Sri Lanka keep themselves alive before collapseSri Lanka's chase did not begin smoothly as they lost an early wicket, but Chamari Athapaththu and Vishmi Gunaratne briefly revived their hopes with a fighting 58-run partnership. Athapaththu looked to take the attack to the Indian bowlers, while Gunaratne provided valuable support. However, with the required run rate climbing rapidly, both batters were forced to take greater risks.The breakthrough came at a crucial stage as Athapaththu was dismissed for 36 before Gunaratne followed for 20 in the same over. Their twin dismissals effectively broke Sri Lanka's resistance and swung the final decisively India's way.India’s spin attack dismantles Sri LankaOnce the partnership was broken, Sri Lanka's middle order simply could not withstand India's relentless bowling attack. The visitors slipped from 63/3 to 103/7 as wickets tumbled in quick succession. India kept attacking the stumps and denied Sri Lanka any opportunity to rebuild the innings.Shree Charani was the star with the ball, finishing with outstanding figures of 4/20 from her four overs. Her spell proved decisive as India continued to squeeze the Sri Lankan batters.Deepti Sharma also played a key role in the bowling effort, adding two crucial wickets to her already impressive tournament tally. She entered the final among the leading wicket-takers of the competition, with 11 wickets in four matches.Sri Lanka were eventually bowled out for 111 on the final ball of their innings, falling 72 runs short of India's imposing target.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Yankees secure September Subway Series as Schlittler stars, Rice and Wells go yard
articles.summary: Schlittler was close to untouchable in rubber game gem against the Mets.
articles.body:
Earlier this week , my colleague Josh asked whether Cam Schlittler could join Justin Verlander and Clayton Kershaw as the only pitchers this century to win MVP. With each successive appearance like this one, Josh's question begins to look more and more prescient. Schlittler was close to untouchable, allowing just one hit across six scoreless innings to hold serve with Dylan Cease in the AL Cy Young race. Ben Rice and Austin Wells provided all the offense with a pair of early solo home runs to right as the Yankees won the rubber game, 2-0, to secure this edition of the Subway Series (and a 3-3 split for 2026 as a whole).

Christian Scott entered this game as one of the best pitcher's in the NL when it came to his team's record in his starts, which made it important that the Yankees get on the board early. He offers a rare blend of swing and miss and damage limitation, so it was encouraging to see Rice really get into a 1-2 splitter, lining it just over the wall in right for a classic Yankee Stadium porch job.

As if you needed anything more to play for in the midst of a tense divisional race, Schlittler seemed to be pitching with an added edge this afternoon. He is neck-and-neck with Cease in the AL Cy Young race — also starting today against the Orioles — and likely wanted to answer the humiliation the Yankees faced in their drubbing the afternoon prior. He struck out four in the first two innings, three of those coming against a four-seamer that the whole Mets lineup looked nowhere close to catching up to.

Volpe got his first real test in these four games at second base and answered it with aplomb. He ranged well to his right on a sharp Brett Baty grounder, gloving it and making a jump throw to first , this shorter throwing distance seeming to suit Volpe's arm better than having to make a similar throw from in the hole at short. In the bottom of the frame, it was his chicken parm brother's turn to make his mark on this game.

Austin Wells has looked miles more competitive at the plate over the last few months after a truly abysmal start to his season. He's not giving so many pitches away and he's not missing as much when he gets what he is looking for. That being said, he entered today's contest amid an 0-for-20 skid — snapped in loud fashion in his first AB of the game. He ambushed an elevated first-pitch heater at 96 mph, launching it into the second deck in right for his eleventh home run of the year to double the Yankees' lead, 2-0.

With the way Schlittler was dealing, those two runs must have looked like a mountain to climb to the opposition. The Mets didn't manage their first hit off him until two outs into the fifth, Baty pulling a 3-1 cutter into the corner in right for a double before a Nick Morabito grounder stranded him at second.

Other than the pair of solo homers, the Yankees offer much resistance against Scott. José Caballero and Rice drew a pair of walks after the Wells homer but that came to nothing. Otherwise it was pretty smooth sailing for the Mets' second-year starter, who ended with seven strikeouts across his six innings of work including striking out the side in the fifth.

After the contact started to tick up against Schlittler in the fourth and fifth, he answered Scott's striking out of the side by ringing up Francisco Lindor and Juan Soto to open the sixth (aided by a generous check swing strike three call on Soto by the third base umpire). There was then a scary moment as Schlittler took a 112 mph liner from Bo Bichette off the back of his right thigh, the batted ball missing his pitching hand by inches. He was able to walk off the field under his own power, but went straight down the tunnel to end his outing at 94 pitches with Brent Headrick coming out to open the seventh.

If Schlittler can keep stacking starts like this, his Cy Young hopes and his team's playoff outlook will keep on improving. It's his sixth straight outing allowing one or fewer runs, extending his single-season Yankees franchise record to 21 such starts. He had to lean on four-seamer and sinker today, the curveball showing little feel while he wasn't quite able to finish his cutters, leaving a lot out of the zone to the arm-side. This elevated his pitch count to 94, which in addition to the come-backer were likely the reasons Schlittler couldn't go really deep in this start given his stuff showed no signs of degrading in his final inning. Schlittler ends the day having given up a hit and two walks with eight strikeouts in six scoreless innings to lower his season ERA below two for the first time since the first week of July.

As they've done almost without fail since the start of summer, Headrick, Paul Blackburn , and David Bednar slammed the door after Schlittler's day ended. They allowed just two hits and no walks in the final three scoreless innings, the three-headed monster nailing down another victory, 2-0, to secure the series over the crosstown rivals.

The Yankees next fly to Minnesota for three games against the Twins. Will Warren is slated to start the opener, facing off against a familiar face from his days with the Orioles in Dean Kremer . First pitch is scheduled for 7:40 pm ET on Monday with the broadcast remaining on YES.

articles.title: ‘We can’t receive the trophy from him’: Why India snubbed Mohsin Naqvi again at Women’s Asia Cup, Devajit Saikia explains
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India’s women’s cricket team’s decision not to receive the Women’s Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council president Mohsin Naqvi was a .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s women’s cricket team’s decision not to receive the Women’s Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council president Mohsin Naqvi was a show of solidarity with the men’s team, which took the same position after winning the Asia Cup last year, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said.“Our men’s team won the Asia Cup a year and a half ago. And our whole situation, since the April 2025 Pahalgam incident, changed after that. So, after that, there was pressure on us from our citizens that we shouldn’t keep any relations with our neighboring country and not play cricket with them. But our government has a policy that we must play against every country in multinational tournaments...” Saikia told IANS hours after India beat Sri Lanka in Sunday's final.“But that doesn’t mean we will follow every condition laid out for us. Our military conflict is still ongoing. One of the main leaders who is working against the interests of our country; we can’t receive the trophy from him. The Women’s team has expressed solidarity with the decision taken by the men’s team last year,” Saikia said.The decision brought back memories of the controversial presentation after the men's Asia Cup final in 2025. India had beaten Pakistan in the final, but the players were left waiting for more than an hour to receive the trophy and medals.This time, India had completed a comfortable 72-run victory over Sri Lanka to win a record-extending eighth Women's Asia Cup title. Harmanpreet Kaur and her teammates celebrated on the field, but the Indian side did not collect the trophy from Naqvi during the presentation.Naqvi was present at the stadium as India sealed the title and was seated alongside dignitaries including BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla and Saikia. He later went on stage and handed the runners-up cheque to Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu. The presentation then ended without India receiving the trophy from him.Saikia said the decision did not take away from the team's performance.“It doesn’t diminish the performances of our team. We have won all our matches in a one-sided manner. Women’s cricket has been growing so well in India and there’s no bigger evidence of that than this. Our whole planning is geared towards the 2026 ICC T20 World Cup. The happiest part of this tournament is how India has left everyone else behind and surged so far ahead.”The presence of Naqvi alongside Saikia and Shukla in the Royal Box during the match also led to questions about the interaction between the officials.“It’s not as if we wouldn’t meet anyone. I was sitting outside in the Royal Box seats right from the toss until the end of the game. Having sat there, I remained in that same place throughout the match. Everyone who came met me during the match; someone sat next to me, then Shukla came and sat with me. The person you mentioned also came and sat alongside Deputy Chairman Khalid (Khalid Al Zarooni) sahib. That’s just a normal tradition—whenever anyone comes, we meet and talk with everyone,” Saikia said.Saikia said there had been an attempt to resolve the trophy presentation issue.“We tried to solve today's situation, but our efforts were not successful. We don’t have any regrets. Our ultimate priority and ambition was not to focus on who would give the trophy. We wanted the Indian team to win and we’ve achieved that.”He also said his interaction with Naqvi was not centred on the trophy. Saikia had presented the fielding medal after the game and said the conversation around that was about India's next assignment.“I also got the chance to give the fielding medal that’s given out after every game. The conversation that was had around that was about the Asian Games, not about whether the trophy should be taken or not.”India's attention now shifts to the Asian Games in Japan's Aichi Prefecture. The team is scheduled to play on September 18, 20 and 22.“Currently, there are no such plans. Right now, our focus is on tomorrow, as our team will be leaving for Japan via Delhi. So, all our attention is set on the Asian Games starting in Japan, where our matches are scheduled for the 18th, 20th and 22nd. Our goal is to bring home the gold medal, and that is our sole objective.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

We stand by it. For us, this tournament is over. We are the champions. That's good enough. This tournament is over. Officially over for us,” Muzumdar told reporters after the final.“It was on the big board that India, the champions of Asia Cup 2026. We are happy that we've turned out to be champions. For us, this tournament is officially over. The fact that we're champions, we're really glad, and I'm really proud of every single person in this unit, including the support staff and the players, needless to say. We're looking forward to the Asian Games now,” he said.The controversy did little to overshadow India’s commanding performance in the final.India dominate Sri Lanka to win eighth titleAfter being asked to bat first, India posted a formidable 183/5, with openers Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma producing a record-breaking start. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi on the bench: Why India's bold T20I vision feels incomplete
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India T20I skipper Shreyas Iyer called having to pick between Sanju Samson, Vaibhav Sooryanshi and Abhishek Sharma as a \"luxury to have for.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India T20I skipper Shreyas Iyer called having to pick between Sanju Samson, Vaibhav Sooryanshi and Abhishek Sharma as a "luxury to have for any side." More often than not, the challenge is to pick between Samson and Sooryavanshi. One brings experience, and the other brings a no-holds-barred approach.That was the case as the T20I series between India and Afghanistan got underway on Sunday at the Arun Jaitley Stadium. No clear signs of one or the other emerged as the teams went through the motions. Abhishek did some shadow batting. Sooryavanshi lined up to take some aerial catches. India coach Gautam Gambhir pinged Samson's wicketkeeping gloves.As the team went into a huddle and emerged, both Samson and Sooryavanshi found their way onto the dugout. Both kept their poker faces well. Ishan Kishan, one of the wicketkeeping options in the squad, spoke for a considerable period with batting coach Sitanshu Kotak.The mystery box was opened at the toss when Shreyas Iyer announced that Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Washington Sundar and two more (Ravi Bishnoi and Yash Thakur) were not in the playing XI. His reasoning to Sanjay Manjrekar was near incoherent."That is more difficult, I feel, but I would say if Vaibhav (Sooryavanshi) is not playing, then Washington (Sundar) is not playing and there are two more which you'll get to know," he said on managing team combinations and selecting players for the match.When it came to it, Sanju Samson scored just 10 runs from 8 balls with two boundaries to show for it. His brief stay in the middle was halted by Azmatullah Omarzai, giving catching practice to Darwish Rasooli at deep square leg in the process. On a surface that needed patience before getting going, as Abhishek Sharma demonstrated with a 32-ball 82, the 31-year-old had not made the most of the opportunity.The question of batting order that Iyer didn't answer with conviction at the toss was probed again with Abhishek Sharma and Varun Chakaravarthy after India's 7-wicket win with 38 balls to spare."I still remember two years back, we decided we want to play a certain way and dominate all teams. It worked for a year. But one or two (bad) series won't define our batting. As openers, you want to give a good start as an opener," said Sharma, whose 82-run knock earned him the Player of the Match.Varun, meanwhile, praised India's top order for how lethal they are against spinners."Against our team, batting line-up, you can't bowl spin. So, if you bowl spin against our batting line-up, they are just going to smack (you) left, right and centre. We are so used to playing spinners. We have one of the best batting line-ups and our top-8 can take on any spinner in the world. I have personally bowled against them, played against them. I know how hard it is. So, yeah, I feel for the spinners," said the spinner who had an economical return from injury.The question, however, persists over Sooryavanshi's place in the team and the long-term approach in the format. Samson's presence adds a wicketkeeping option and a left-right pairing at the top of the order. But, with all due respect to Samson's abilities, it steals what can be a game-changing and game-deciding pairing of Abhishek-Sooryavanshi.Samson posted single-digit scores against Ireland and in the first T20I against England before allowing Sooryavanshi to come in and make his India debut. Sooryavanshi couldn't do much either, with 42 runs from three matches.But as Samson was rested for the tour to Zimbabwe and Sooryavanshi became the de facto choice, the 15-year-old produced a series-topping 151 runs from three matches at a strike rate of 196.10.With India set to play two T20Is against Afghanistan, a one-off T20I against Japan, the Asian Games, five T20Is against West Indies, five T20Is against New Zealand and three T20Is against Sri Lanka in 2026, the can of worms involving Sooryavanshi has been opened with his absence.The sole reason Sooryavanshi was included in squads for Ireland and England, and fast-tracked into the Indian team at all of 15, was to give wings to this sensational talent. Not playing him, in favour of Samson's experience, does grave disservice to him, his talent and Indian cricket at large.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

Our military conflict is still ongoing. One of the main leaders who is working against the interests of our country; we can’t receive the trophy from him. The Women’s team has expressed solidarity with the decision taken by the men’s team last year,” Saikia said.However, television cameras showed Saikia meeting Naqvi during the match. As players shook hands after the final, the broadcast showed the Royal Box at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, where Naqvi first greeted BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla and then had a conversation with Saikia.Asked about that meeting, Saikia said it was part of normal match-day protocol and did not contradict the BCCI's stand on the trophy presentation."It's not as if we wouldn't meet anyone. I was sitting outside in the Royal Box seats right from the toss until the end of the game. Having sat there, I remained in that same place throughout the match. Everyone who came met me during the match; someone sat next to me, then Rajeev Shukla came and sat with me. The person you mentioned (Naqvi) also came and sat alongside deputy chairman Khalid Sahib. That's just a normal tradition—whenever anyone comes, we meet and talk with everyone."It may be recalled that the Indian men’s team had last year declined to receive the Asia Cup trophy and medals from Naqvi, who heads the Pakistan Cricket Board and is also the Interior Minister of that country.The Indian team is yet to receive the Asia Cup trophy, which has since been kept in the ACC office.Instead the Suryakumar Yadav-led Indian side conducted an impromptu celebration on the dais without the physical prize.However, this time the Indian women’s team members did not even return to the ground after BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia presented Nandini Sharma with an in-house best fielder medal.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India thrive in home comfort: Bumrah hits stride on comeback as Iyer’s men crush Afghanistan in first T20I
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Jasprit Bumrah’s first delivery of the night drifted past Rahmanullah Gurbaz’s pads and beat wicketkeeper Sanju Samson to the boundary for .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Jasprit Bumrah’s first delivery of the night drifted past Rahmanullah Gurbaz’s pads and beat wicketkeeper Sanju Samson to the boundary for five wides. That was the only time one could say he was coming off an injury layoff. Two deliveries later, he got the ball to kick from a good length for Gurbaz to awkwardly fend it to first slip. From there, usual business resumed for India’s T20I team on home soil after a winless tour of Ireland and England two months ago.The Indian bowling attack, led by Bumrah, stifled Afghanistan to 156/8.Opener Abhishek Sharma effortlessly blazed away to 82 off 32 and Ishan Kishan eased to 42 off 33 as India cantered to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match series with seven wickets and 38 balls to spare with captain Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma completing the formalities at the Arun Jaitley Stadium on Sunday evening.On paper, Afghanistan are the hosts of this T20I series. But the Indian T20I team re-established this as their hunting ground. As is often the case with Bumrah, that one menacing delivery to Gurbaz shook the confidence of the Afghanistan batting. And as usual, Bumrah set the tone for the rest of the attack to settle down on a length against an unsure batting lineup.Call it the impact of Bumrah’s spell of 1/26 or playing in Indian conditions, India’s new T20I captain Iyer finally got to see how ominous this team can be after taking over the reins from Suryakumar Yadav post the T20 World Cup triumph at home.Azmatullah Omarzai’s enterprising unbeaten 64 off 44 balls dragged Afghanistan out of the ditch at 43/5 to post 156/8. Bumrah’s arrival just goes to show the difference he makes to an attack.Going by their records, Arshdeep Singh, Axar Patel and Varun Chakravarthy were expected to have the upper hand against a comparatively inexperienced Afghan batting lineup. That said, this same attack without Bumrah came second in all six T20Is on the tour of Ireland and England. The incisive opening burst allowed Arshdeep, Axar and Varun to apply the choke as they returned figures of 3/19, 1/27 and 1/16.Bumrah has predominantly played T20 cricket over last year. Most of it has been on scary flat decks. Sunday’s pitch at the Ferozeshah Kotla was a tired one after enduring the load of the IPL and Delhi Premier League T20.Help of any kind from the surface is enough for Bumrah to get into the minds of the batters. From letting it rip with the new ball to using the dual nature of the pitch with his cutters, he flaunted his wares in his first T20 game after the IPL. If one crack in India’s T20 cricket stood exposed on Sunday night, it was the lack of decent bowling allrounder. Even as Omarzai went about rebuilding the innings with veteran Mohammed Nabi, the run rate dipped below six runs per over by the 10th over with India’s frontline bowlers operating with immaculate accuracy. The shackles were broken only when seamers Nitish Kumar Reddy and Shivam Dube were taken for 0/30 in two overs and 21 off one over respectively.Brief scores: Afghanistan 156-8 in 20 overs (Azmatullah Omarzai 64 not out, Mohammad Nabi 33; Arshdeep Singh 3-19, Varun Chakravarthy 1-16) lost to India 157-3 in 13.4 overs (Abhishek Sharma 82, Ishan Kishan 42; Mohammad Nabi 2-28) by seven wickets.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Women’s Asia Cup: Shafali, Smriti’s stunning opening act powers India to eighth title
articles.summary: Cricket News: At last, India got a batting beauty and made the most of it, thanks to their in-form openers Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana. Continuing her blazing.
articles.body: At last, India got a batting beauty and made the most of it, thanks to their in-form openers Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana. Continuing her blazing form, Shafali smashed 68 off 39, adding 129 in just 77 balls with fellow superstar and vice-captain Mandhana (59 off 39), who also stroked a half-century, as India defeated defending champions Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Women’s Asia Cup final to clinch a record eighth title at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Sunday. Shree Charani snapped four wickets to hasten Sri Lanka’s downfall.In a murderous mood, Shafali took just 24 balls to reach her 21st fifty, erasing Mandhana’s 25-ball effort in 2022 as the fastest fifty in Women’s Asia Cup history. Mandhana reached her 36th T20I half century in 35 balls. Given the start they got, India would be disappointed at not reaching 200 after a middle-order muddle. Skipper Harmanpreet Kaur (14, 14b, 1x4), Richa Ghosh (17, 13b, 1x4, 1x6) and Deepti Sharma (5, 7b) fell cheaply as Sri Lanka staged a fine fightback.India recovered towards the end through a fine cameo from G Kamalini (15*, 5b, 1x4, 1x6), who was surprisingly included in the XI after India dropped out-of-form No. 3 Pratika Rawal. Kamalini skipped down the track to edge Sugandika Kumari for four before finishing the innings in style by dancing down the track and depositing the bowler over cow corner. Sri Lanka also suffered a major blow when batter Vishmi Gunarathne was stretchered off after twisting her ankle while fielding. The injury leaves the pressure of a stiff 184-run chase on captain Chamari Athapaththu and her team.Shafali, who cracked her third half century of the tournament — all three scores have been in the 60s — and Mandhana took the Sri Lankan attack to the cleaners on perhaps the best batting surface of the tournament. With 236 runs in five matches at 47.20 and a strike rate of 171.01, Shafali is set to finish as the tournament’s leading run-scorer. Mandhana, with 213 runs at 42.60 and a strike rate of 165.11, is set to finish second.Shafali targeted Athapaththu in the latter’s first over, creaming her for 6, 6 and 4 as the Sri Lankan skipper conceded 20 runs. India raced to 57 in the Powerplay and reached 98 at the halfway mark without losing a wicket. Much to Sri Lanka’s relief, the stand ended when Shafali slapped Praboda straight to Athapaththu at the edge of the circle.Mandhana, though, would be disappointed to have been run out for the third time in this Asia Cup. In a debatable decision, she sacrificed her wicket in the 14th over after Harmanpreet cut a ball to point and set off, leaving her partner with little option but to go through with the run. It was a poor call by Harmanpreet, though Mandhana could have turned it down.Brief scores: India Women 183/5 in 20 overs (S Verma 68, S Mandhana 59; C Praboda 1/40) beat Sri Lanka Women 111 all out in 20 overs (C Athapaththu 36, N Silva 22; S Charani 4-20, D Sharma 3-19) by 72 runs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 15 vs 3.33: How struggling England side swept Pakistan 3-0
articles.summary: Cricket News: Joe Root was on 23, England were 36 for two and chasing 130 in the final Test at Edgbaston when an expansive cover drive crashed into his leg stump. M.
articles.body: Joe Root was on 23, England were 36 for two and chasing 130 in the final Test at Edgbaston when an expansive cover drive crashed into his leg stump. Mohammad Ali was already running away in celebration before he turned around to see the umpire's arm stretched out for a front-foot no-ball. It was his 17th such offence in the series, but the first one that had cost him a wicket. England would have been 36 for three; instead, they won the match by eight wickets and completed a 3-0 sweep over Pakistan.There was something fitting about the way the series ended. Pakistan lost a wicket on the first ball of the series and, on the last ball, misfielded as England completed the whitewash. In between, there had been three Tests in which Pakistan rarely looked competitive, often looked unprepared and, by the end, barely resembled (literally) the team that had landed in England.Less than 24 hours after Pakistan's heavy defeat in the second at Lord's had sealed the series for England, the PCB announced that seven players had been axed from the Test squad. Quietly tucked into the final line of the statement was the news that head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed, who had been in the job for only five games, had also been "released" along with fast bowling coach Umar Gul. They were replaced by Pakistan's white-ball coaches Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke.The seven players brought into the squad included five with no Test experience and another two who had played a combined 10 Tests. By the time Pakistan reached Birmingham, they were not only playing a different group of players from the one that had begun the tour, they were also in many ways no longer playing a Test team at all.The upheaval continued when Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq, two of the players removed from the squad, were investigated by Pakistan's National Cyber Crimes Investigation Agency (NCCIA) over allegations of leaking team information.None of this is unfamiliar territory for Pakistan cricket. The Test side has had three captains and six head coaches in the last three years, while the PCB has gone through five chairmen in five years.Punishing players has often gone hand in hand with those changes.The PCB banned then-captain Mohammad Yousuf and senior batter Younis Khan for an indefinite period and disciplined five other players, including Afridi, after a disastrous 3-0 whitewash in Australia in 2010.The defeat at Edgbaston was Pakistan's 16th in their last 21 Tests and left them ninth and last in the current World Test Championship (WTC) cycle, the same position in which they finished the previous cycle.An average England team did not need to be greatPakistan's performance in the series was not even average. If there was a team that played average cricket, it was England. Pakistan were below average.England did not need to have a great series to win it. No batter from either side scored a century in the series, while one of England's four fast bowlers, Gus Atkinson, took only four wickets in the entire series, three of them in the final innings.England's numbers 8 to 11 averaged more than Pakistan's top seven. Before Pakistan's second innings in the final Test, the only time they crossed 200 in the series, Tongue had already hit as many boundaries (11) as any Pakistani batter other than Saud Shakeel.Pakistan's first innings score in the three Tests tells much of the story: 171 at Leeds, 110 at Lord's and 133 at Birmingham. They were repeatedly so far behind after their first innings that the second half of the match became an exercise in trying to recover from damage that had already been done.England's opening pair averaged less than 15 runs together across the series, which should have given Pakistan an advantage. However, Pakistan’s openers managed only 3.33 in the series. Moreover, their first two wickets averaged just 4.66 runs. Across six innings, they scored only 56 runs for their first two wickets, the worst average for the first two wickets by any team in a Test series where they batted in at least five innings.At Lord's, Imam-ul-Haq injured his calf on the first day and did not even bat in either innings. So England's biggest weakness in the series didn't really become a weakness.Pakistan used 23 players on the tour, with 16 of them eventually playing. On the other hand, England used 11 players across the three Tests.Pakistan also bowled 38 no-balls compared with England's eight, another telling difference in a series where the margin between the two sides was often created by their ability to get ordinary things right.This was the sixth time in 12 series that Pakistan had been whitewashed in a Test series of two or more matches in the last four years.Saud Shakeel showed some resistance when everyone around him seemed keen to return to the dressing room, finishing the series as the second-highest scorer from either side. Mohammad Abbas was also somewhat consistent with the ball, taking 13 wickets at an average of 25.38. There were moments of brilliance from Razaullah in the third Test, who came in as a replacement for one of the seven players axed after Lord’s. But that was all: moments. Pakistan look in no position to get better from here, while the PCB, going by its pattern, looks set to continue operating on its annual panic cycle.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Watch: ‘Good job sir’ — Pakistan fan praises Mohsin Naqvi after Team India snubs trophy at Women’s Asia Cup
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India’s record eighth Women’s Asia Cup title was followed by a trophy presentation that quickly became the biggest talking point of the fin.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s record eighth Women’s Asia Cup title was followed by a trophy presentation that quickly became the biggest talking point of the final — and a video from outside the Dubai International Cricket Stadium has now added another twist to the controversy.A video circulating on social media shows Asian Cricket Council president and Pakistan Cricket Board chairman Mohsin Naqvi leaving the stadium after India defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final on Sunday.As Naqvi’s car passed a Pakistan supporter filming his exit, the fan could be heard praising the PCB chief and backing his handling of the situation involving India.“Good job sir, we are happy with you. They [India] don't deserve this trophy. We love you. You are a great man. You are doing well. Keep it up,” the fan was heard saying in the video.Naqvi, who appeared to smile and wave at the supporters as his car moved past, had earlier been at the centre of the trophy presentation controversy after the Indian players did not come forward to receive the trophy from him.Watch:‘Trophy chor’ chants echo after India snub presentationIndia had completed a dominant 72-run victory over Sri Lanka to win the Women’s Asia Cup for a record-extending eighth time. But when the presentation began, Harmanpreet Kaur and her teammates did not collect the trophy from Naqvi.Naqvi remained on the presentation stage and handed the runners-up cheque to Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu. The Indian players celebrated their title on the field but did not participate in the trophy handover involving the ACC president.As Naqvi subsequently left the stadium, “Trophy chor, trophy chor” chants were heard around the venue.The chants were a callback to the controversy surrounding the men’s Asia Cup final in 2025. India had defeated Pakistan in Dubai, but the trophy and medal presentation was delayed by more than an hour, with visuals showing the Asia Cup trophy being taken away from the presentation area.The episode triggered criticism and trolling aimed at Naqvi, with “Trophy chor” subsequently becoming a recurring phrase used by some Indian supporters.Saikia explains India’s decisionBCCI secretary Devajit Saikia later explained why the Indian players had refused to take the trophy from Naqvi, linking the decision to the position taken by the men’s side after last year’s Asia Cup final.“Our men’s team won the Asia Cup a year and a half ago. And our whole situation, since the April 2025 Pahalgam incident, changed after that. So, after that, there was pressure on us from our citizens that we shouldn’t keep any relations with our neighboring country and not play cricket with them. But our government has a policy that we must play against every country in multinational tournaments...”“But that doesn’t mean we will follow every condition laid out for us. Our military conflict is still ongoing. One of the main leaders who is working against the interests of our country; we can’t receive the trophy from him. The Women’s team has expressed solidarity with the decision taken by the men’s team last year,” Saikia told IANS.Naqvi had been seated in the Royal Box alongside BCCI vice-president Rajiv Shukla and Saikia during the match. Saikia insisted that the interaction between the officials was normal protocol.Saikia also revealed that efforts had been made to resolve the trophy presentation issue.“We tried to solve today's situation, but our efforts were not successful. We don’t have any regrets. Our ultimate priority and ambition was not to focus on who would give the trophy. We wanted the Indian team to win and we’ve achieved that,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kevin Pietersen 'buzzing' at England white-ball coaching role as specialist mentor, says Marcus Trescothick
articles.summary: Kevin Pietersen "buzzing" for England role and will add "a little more spark" to white-ball sides, says batting coach Marcus Trescothick; watch the first T20I against Sri Lanka in Southampton, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 6pm, Tuesday (first ball 6.30pm)
articles.body:
Pietersen will serve as a specialist mentor through to the 2027 Cricket World Cup in Africa next year. He will link up with the squad this week ahead of England's first T20I against Sri Lanka on Tuesday, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 6pm, with the first ball at 6.30pm.

Trescothick and Pietersen were Ashes-winning team-mates during England's famous 2005 triumph, giving the former first-hand experience of the qualities and talents the latter can bring to the current team.

"He is buzzing about putting back on the England shirt or tracksuit, buzzing for the opportunity and it's really exciting," the England batting coach said of Pietersen.

"Having his presence around, and the knowledge he has about batting - he saw batting in a different light to many people - if we can tap into that and get that into our white-ball cricket, It's only going to benefit the team."

Is Pietersen appointment a risk? | 'He'll add a little more spark', says Trescothick

The appointment has raised a few eyebrows, coming 12 years after Pietersen was effectively sacked by the ECB in the wake of England's disastrous 5-0 Ashes drubbing in Australia. At the time, the ECB said he had become "disconnected" from the team and accused him of failing to support then-captain Sir Alastair Cook.

Pietersen had previously been dropped in 2012 after sending text messages to members of the South African team, while he resigned as captain after just five months in 2008 following a breakdown in his relationship with then head coach Peter Moores.

Since his retiring a player in 2018, Pietersen has, at times, also been an outspoken critic of the England setup, including when accusing the white-ball team of inadequate preparation on a tour of India last January after Brendon McCullum had just taken over as head coach, who he'll now be working under.

Having hammered India 4-0 in a T20 series earlier this summer, briefly leapfrogging them at the top of the world rankings, and won their last two ODI series against Sri Lanka and India, England's decision to hire Pietersen appears a risky move at a time when the team is enjoying a strong run of form.

"You can see the team moving in the right direction; we've had great results in the last sort of 18 months - in both formats," Trescothick said, before adding: "I think you're just adding a little more spark and a little bit more variety from a different coach's point of view.

"Kevin has seen white-ball cricket around the world for a long period of time, playing in all the big competitions, he's won a [T20] World Cup [in 2010], you're going to gain something extra.

"It's up to the coaching setup with Brendon to draw out the best from him.

"Management of different players, coaches and setups is is the great art, isn't it? If you get that right, then you get a lot of good things come from coaches and players alike."

articles.title: ‘Focus on wearing your national cap, education, respect your parents and coaches’: Arjuna Ranatunga tells Mumbai' budding cricketers
articles.summary: Cricket News: MUMBAI: Sri Lanka's celebrated 1996 World Cup winning captain Arjuna Ranatunga is in Mumbai these days, on a 'business visit.'Ranatunga arrived in the.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Sri Lanka's celebrated 1996 World Cup winning captain Arjuna Ranatunga is in Mumbai these days, on a 'business visit.'Ranatunga arrived in the city on Friday with his close friend and businessman Venkatesh K Rao. On Saturday, the 62-year-old Lankan great addressed a gathering of budding cricketers and their parents, of the Payyade Sports Club in Kandivli.“I had the privilege of having a good session with young cricketers of Mumbai yesterday. I spoke to them about some of the cricketing values which are missing today. I told them about the value of technique, something that you could see in my playing time with the likes of Sachin Tendulkar, Mohammed Azharuddin, Sourav Ganguly and other top Indian batters,” Ranatunga told TOI on Sunday.The former left-hander, who scored 5105 runs in 93 Tests, asserted that it was important to teach today’s young cricketers about the value of playing for the country, rather than only focus on raking in moolah by playing in cash-rich franchise T20 leagues.“It's important to bring these kids on the right track. Today's cricketers look to play in the franchise leagues, rather than playing for their country. They are looking at the financial benefits, rather than taking pride in wearing the cap and jersey of your national team. If you look at it, a couple of Sri Lankan cricketers missed Sri Lanka's series recently to play in franchise cricket, and in India's case too, cricketers are prioritising playing for their franchises.The cricket boards also need to look at the need of their cricketers playing for the country. I'm not saying get rid of T20 cricket, but back in Colombo too, I look to emphasize on the importance of educating the budding cricketers about the value of playing Test cricket," Ranatunga explained."It is the seniors who need to show the way, make a little bit of sacrifice. So, we emphasized on that. Dr Shetty also has the same ideas that I carry. Before I started my speech, he said a lot of things that I was supposed to mention in my speech. Both of us spoke about the value of wearing the national cap, maintaining discipline, the value of education and technique, respecting your parents and coaches-those are the things that are missing in cricket today, and we need to educate the kids about it," he stressed."I enjoyed talking to the cricketers, they listened to me very attentively. We were lucky that growing up, we had our role models in Sunil Gavaskar and Gundappa Viswanath.When we went to Pakistan, we saw some fine cricketing brains like Imran Khan, Javed Miandad and Abdul Qadir. When I played a Test for the first time in India, in Chennai, Gavaskar took time out for us and spoke to us in our dressing room after the match. I will always cherish his words that day," Ranatunga said."It was a very good session, which lasted for 90 minutes. He was talking about cricket and how to respect parents and how to leave the house with the blessing of your parents. He also told the kids to focus on studies. He told the cricketers that they should focus on education too because today, a cricketer has to be intelligent as well. He emphasized to the aspiring cricketers that studies and parents' respect is very important," Payyade Sports Club president and former MCA joint secretary PV Shetty told Mumbai Mirror.Gaurav Payyade, former MCA apex council member and secretary of Payyade SC, and Bhushan Patil, member of MCA’s present Apex Council, were also present on the occasion."We wanted him to speak to the boys at the ground, but it was raining. So, he spoke to the young cricketers of our club at my hotel in Kandivali. He is keen to establish a cricket academy in Mumbai in collaboration with me," Shetty said.Ranataunga and Venkatesh will leave for Rajkot on Wednesday as they have to visit Morbi for business purposes.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakistan’s England nightmare deepens: 11 WTC points docked, 50% match fee fine — here’s why
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Pakistan’s disastrous 0-3 Test series defeat against England has been compounded by a significant over-rate penalty, with the side losing 1.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Pakistan’s disastrous 0-3 Test series defeat against England has been compounded by a significant over-rate penalty, with the side losing 11 World Test Championship points and being fined 50 per cent of their match fee following the Edgbaston Test.Pakistan were found to be 11 overs short of the required over-rate during the third and final Test in Birmingham, which England won by eight wickets to complete a 3-0 series sweep.“Pakistan have been hit with a pair of sanctions for maintaining a slow over-rate during the third and final ICC World Test Championship contest against England in Birmingham,” the ICC said.11-point deduction and maximum fineRanjan Madugalle of the Emirates ICC Elite Panel of Match Referees imposed the sanction after on-field umpires Paul Reiffel and Chris Gaffaney, third umpire Allahudien Palekar and fourth umpire Russell Warren levelled the charge.Pakistan captain Babar Azam pled guilty to the offence and accepted the proposed sanction, meaning there was no need for a formal hearing.The deduction further dents Pakistan’s position at the bottom of the WTC standings, leaving them ninth with a points percentage of 4.63.Under Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, players are fined five per cent of their match fee for every over their side fails to bowl within the allotted time, with the maximum penalty capped at 50 per cent.“In accordance with Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to minimum over-rate offences, players are fined five per cent of their match fee for each over their team fails to bowl within the allotted time, with the maximum penalty capped at 50 percent of the match fee.”The 11-over shortfall also resulted in an 11-point deduction under the WTC playing conditions.“In addition, as per Article 16.11.2 of the ICC World Test Championship playing conditions, a side is penalised one point for each over short. Consequently, 11 World Test Championship points have been deducted from Pakistan’s points total,” the ICC said.ALSO READ: 15 vs 3.33: How struggling England side swept Pakistan 3-0England complete 3-0 sweepThe penalty adds to a miserable WTC campaign for Pakistan, who have recorded just two wins and seven defeats from nine Tests and now languish ninth in the standings.England completed the series sweep with an eight-wicket victory at Edgbaston. Pakistan were bowled out for 133 in their first innings before England posted 453, taking a 320-run lead.Pakistan fought back with 449 in their second innings, with Shan Masood scoring 95, Babar making 76 and debutant Razaullah hitting 81. Razaullah and Mohammad Abbas added 121 for the ninth wicket.But England needed only 130 and reached 130/2, with Joe Root unbeaten on 62 and Jordan Cox on 59.England had earlier won the series opener at Headingley by an innings and 103 runs and the second Test at Lord’s by 194 runs.Pakistan’s next WTC assignment comes in November when they host Sri Lanka for a two-Test series in Rawalpindi and Lahore.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Once in a lifetime’: Pakistan’s Salman Ali Agha answers England setback with maiden triple century
articles.summary: Cricket News: Just days after being sent home from Pakistan’s England tour following a disappointing start to the Test series, Salman Ali Agha has responded in emph.
articles.body: Just days after being sent home from Pakistan’s England tour following a disappointing start to the Test series, Salman Ali Agha has responded in emphatic fashion — with a monumental maiden first-class triple century.The Pakistan batter smashed an unbeaten 300 for Kingsmen Academy against Markhor IT Solutions in the President’s Trophy Grade-I, producing a statement innings after his omission became one of the major talking points in Pakistan cricket.Salman reached the landmark from 336 balls, hitting 42 fours and six sixes, as Kingsmen Academy declared their first innings at 565/7 in 131.1 overs at the Abbottabad Cricket Stadium.The 32-year-old also shared a mammoth 274-run partnership with Mohammad Suleman, who scored 115 off 219 balls, including 13 fours and two sixes.Salman’s extraordinary response came only days after he was sent home from England following Pakistan’s defeat in the second Test at Lord’s.‘My form has not been good’Salman had entered the England tour as part of Pakistan’s Test plans and even stood in as captain in the first Test at Headingley after Babar Azam suffered an arm injury during the tour match.But his own batting struggles continued. He scored only 25 runs across two innings as Pakistan suffered an innings-and-103-run defeat at Headingley. He subsequently lost his place in the XI for the Lord’s Test and was among seven players released from the squad ahead of the third Test as Pakistan made sweeping changes after falling 0-2 behind in the series.His domestic comeback could hardly have been more emphatic.After scoring an unbeaten 101 on the opening day of the President’s Trophy, Salman returned on Sunday to turn his century into a triple century.In a video released by the Pakistan Cricket Board, Salman credited adjustments to his batting for the remarkable turnaround.“My form in international cricket has not been up to the mark in the last few series. I made slight adjustments to my batting, and I’m happy because such milestones are once in a lifetime,” Salman said.“I like to play domestic cricket, and I enjoy coming back to it, as I had spent 10 years here before graduating to the top level. I dedicate this innings to my family. My form has not been good. It was a challenging time, so I dedicate this innings to them,” he added.Salman’s innings came as Pakistan’s domestic competition provided him with the perfect platform to rebuild his confidence.Salman’s triple ton puts Kingsmen in commandKingsmen Academy, playing in their maiden first-class tournament, resumed Sunday at 257/3 and eventually declared at 565/7 immediately after Salman completed his triple century.Markhor IT Solutions finished the day on 179/3, still 386 runs behind.Mohammad Farooq provided an explosive response with an unbeaten 107 off just 95 balls, including 11 fours and five sixes. articles.title: Australia's Steve Smith on 2027 Ashes series in England: 'I don't even know if I'll be there yet'
articles.summary: Steve Smith has a superb Test record in England - but will he still be around for Ashes series next summer? Australia batter laments dwindling role for spinners in Test cricket and says some wobble-seam deliveries are "just unplayable"; Australia face South Africa this autumn
articles.body:
Smith will turn 38 a couple of weeks before the first Test at Trent Bridge next June.

The batter has never won an Ashes series away from home and the 2027 contest would surely represent his last chance to do so.

Speaking to The Telegraph , Smith said: "I don't even know if I'll be there yet. I'm kind of a series-by-series proposition, as I've been for a while. That's still a fair way away for me right now.

"I'd love to win [an Ashes in England] but you wait and see if that comes to fruition."

Smith's Test record in England is stellar - an average of 54.27 across 23 matches with his haul of 2,334 runs including eight hundreds and 10 half-centuries.

The right-hander averaged a shade over 50 across his nine Test outings in 2025, while in three games this year - one against England and two versus Bangladesh - he is averaging 61.40.

He said: "I feel I'm batting really nicely. I've found different ways to go about things on these tricky surfaces and still be able to score runs.

"So trying to contribute as well as I can for the team, score runs, take catches, help out in leadership areas where I need to - it's been a good, fun couple of years."

Smith - who is eager to prolong his T20 career and play for Australia in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics - also had his say on how bowlers perfecting the wobble-seam delivery in Test cricket is making life incredibly difficult for batters.

He said: "There are some balls now that are just unplayable. Some of these balls have your name on it and you can't do anything about it.

"If it's seaming two degrees, you're not hitting that ball, or you shouldn't be hitting that ball. If you're hitting it, you're probably not a very good batter, to be honest. You're playing down the wrong line.

"And if it's coming into you, and it's hitting the top of the stumps and you're getting trapped in front, you can't do anything about it."

England did not play a frontline spinner during their recent 3-0 home sweep of Pakistan with part-time tweaker Dan Lawrence supporting the four-pronged pace attack of Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue, Jofra Archer and Gus Atkinson.

For Australia, Nathan Lyon is not always a certain pick now due to seam-friendly conditions.

Smith added: "When the ball's moving as much as it is, and you can create relentless pressure by bowlers just continually hitting the spot, spin's by far the easiest thing to face and the thing that you can score freely off.

"It's a shame that we've had such spicy wickets that it's got to that point, because I love playing a spinner. I love watching spin bowlers bowl. I was a spin bowler myself back in the day.

"I'd love to see spin play much more of a part in Test cricket again."

Australia's next red-ball assignment is a three-match series in South Africa from October 9 - the first time they have tackled the Proteas away from home since the ball-tampering scandal in 2018 which led to bans for Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft.
