articles.title: Pakistan fined and docked 11 WTC points for slow over-rate in final test against England
articles.summary: Pakistan was sanctioned on Monday for maintaining a slow over-rate during its eight-wicket loss in the third and final test against England.  The Internation...
articles.body:
ISLAMABAD (AP) — Pakistan was sanctioned on Monday for maintaining a slow over-rate during its eight-wicket loss in the third and final test against England.

The International Cricket Council said in a statement that Pakistan was ruled to be 11 overs short of the target after time allowances were taken into consideration during the Edgbaston test that ended on Saturday.

As a result, Pakistan was fined 50% of its match fee and received an 11-point deduction in the World Test Championship cycle.

The ICC said match referee Ranjan Madugalle imposed the sanction after on-field umpires Paul Reiffel and Chris Gaffaney, third umpire Allahudien Palekar and fourth umpire Russell Warren leveled the charge.

Pakistan is at the bottom of the WTC table after winning just two of its nine test matches. It has two more series to play in this cycle, against Sri Lanka in November and against New Zealand in March 2027.

Pakistan also finished last in the previous WTC cycle and changed its captain after losing 2-0 to Bangladesh earlier this year. However, things worsened during its tour of England with selectors axing seven players after the team lost the second test by an innings and 194 runs at Headingley.

Senior players Salman Ali Agha, Imam-ul-Haq and Mohammad Rizwan were sent home after the second test before England completed the 3-0 sweep.

articles.title: 'Want to play as much T20 cricket as I can': Steve Smith unsure of playing next Ashes series but wants to compete at LA Olympics
articles.summary: With the 2028 Olympics all set to feature cricket for the first time, Steve Smith wants to represent the Aussies at the event even as he remains unsure about...
articles.body:
Steve Smith says he does not know if he will play in next summer's Ashes series in England.

The Australian batter's primary remaining ambition is to represent his country at the 2028 LA Olympics.

He is currently playing for Amsterdam Flames in the European T20 Premier League to stay sharp in the format.

Steve Smith is unsure of playing next in the Ashes series but wants to compete at the LA Olympics

Few batters of the modern era have made themselves as synonymous with Test cricket as Steve Smith. The former Australia skipper has spent 15 years as the core of the Aussies' top order, and in over 41 Tests, he has remained one of the names the English fear most. But now at 37, that magic still seems to be working.

With 13 centuries and 3703 runs at an average of 56.10, his legacy in both the Ashes and Test cricket has long been cemented. And as the 2027 Ashes draw closer, Australia is bound to knock on his door to help them retain the urn once again. But this time, Smith isn't sure he has the answer to the English question.

Speaking to The Telegraph while playing for Amsterdam Flames in the European T20 Premier League, Smith made it clear that winning a maiden Ashes series in England isn't enough to continue his Test career. An away Ashes win might be the only thing left for Smith to win, but it seems he isn't even interested in winning it.

Why Steve Smith is unsure about playing the 2027 Ashes in England

He remained candid when asked if he will be there in England to make it happen. "I don't even know if I'll be there yet," Smith said, admitting he could retire from Test cricket before next summer arrives. He stressed that he's not thinking that far ahead for now. "I'm kind of a series-by-series proposition, as I've been for a while, and that's still a fair way away for me right now," he said.

He admitted that winning an away Ashes series is still on his bucket list. But that's not on top of that list. He continued, "So, yeah, I'd love to win one there or to have won one there, but you wait and see if that comes to fruition." Instead, his clearest remaining target in the game lies way below the Ashes.

With cricket returning to the Olympics for the first time in 128 years at Los Angeles in 2028, with six men's and women's T20 sides competing, Smith, who turns 39 shortly before the Games, is determined to be involved. "Right now probably it's just the Olympics to try to be a part of that," Smith said of his remaining ambitions.

It also gave him a chance to brush up on his T20 play. "One of the reasons why I wanted to play with Amsterdam here was just to continue playing as much T20 cricket as I can," Smith said. It also gave him the chance to learn more about new markets while allowing him to impart some knowledge to associate nation members and players.

Why Smith's uncertainty says more about the schedule than his form

But beyond his Olympic ambitions, there don't seem to be any other reasons for him to put Test cricket on hold for now.

He remains number two on the Test rankings, only behind Harry Brook, and maintains an average of 49.4 over the last two years. That keeps him the best batter the Aussies can have despite his age.

For Smith, age or fitness isn't the reason he wants to avoid looking too far into his future in the longest format; rather, he wants to give it time. Committing to a series that's months away while splitting his focus on multiple goals will only dilute his performance in any of them.

With an opportunity to make it to the squad that gets sent to the USA, extra focus on franchise cricket will only help him keep himself ready for the shortest format.

If Smith does walk away from Test cricket before next summer, it will simply be the end of a career that has seen Smith win every trophy possible and then some.

articles.title: County Championship: Notts, Somerset and Warwickshire vie for title
articles.summary: Somerset, Nottinghamshire and Warwickshire are separated by just five points with two matches of the 2026 County Championship to go.
articles.body:
With two games left of cricket's County Championship, three teams are separated by only five points vying to be the champion team of 2026.

Somerset, Nottinghamshire and Warwickshire enter the final straight all with realistic hopes of holding the trophy on Sunday, 27 September.

None of the sides play each other, so attention will have to be spread across six matches in the final two rounds to see who comes out on top when the music stops.

Throw in bonus points, and those imponderables of possible rain and bad light - and even the toss of a coin - and it's impossible to work out quite where this title race is going to go.

Somerset could be champions this week if they win and Notts and Warwickshire both lose, yet they could be third by Friday night and outsiders. It really is that close.

Let's start with the current leaders and the most romantic tale of all - Somerset. One of only three counties never to have been crowned champions, this is the holy grail.

Think of Boston Red Sox's 'Curse of the Bambino' 86-year wait between World Series titles, Hibernian's 114-year yearning to win the Scottish Cup again, Mayo's success in the All-Ireland Gaelic Football in July after 11 successive defeats in the final. Somerset's quest for the County Championship is of a similar ilk.

They had that great team in the late 1970s and early 1980s of Ian Botham, Joel Garner and Viv Richards which amassed plenty of one-day glory, while in recent years, there has been T20 Blast success.

But the Championship - the standard bearer for the county game - has remained elusive, and in a cricket-mad town like Taunton, excitement is building once again.

Of course, they have been close before. Between 2001 and 2019, they finished runners-up on no fewer than six occasions in the title race.

Tom Abell, Lewis Gregory, Craig Overton and Jack Leach were all part of that last side to come second and they remain integral members of the team now.

Overton has had an outstanding season with ball and bat, but he is wise enough to know the pitfalls of looking too far ahead.

"There's still a long way to go in this Championship and so much cricket to be played," he told BBC Radio Somerset.

"We've just got to keep doing our thing, keep doing the basics and see where we are at the end of this game."

Nottinghamshire were the underdogs 12 months ago as they prevented Surrey from winning four titles in a row, including a memorable victory at The Kia Oval.

This season, they have been the side to beat as they try to become the first Notts side to retain the title.

Joe Clarke has been the stand-out batter on the county circuit with a whopping 1,240 runs, almost 300 more than anyone else in Division One, while the bowling attack led by Olly Stone and Dillon Pennington has caused problems for all batting sides.

However, a failure to beat struggling Leicestershire earlier this month allowed Somerset to nip ahead of them and a tense 54-run success over Hampshire kept the margin between the top two at four points.

"We all knew coming into this week what was needed to really keep us amongst it heading into the two final games," said Stone, who took 9-95 in the Hampshire win at Trent Bridge.

"We go to Sussex now and they're playing good cricket at the moment and then we come back home against Yorkshire when we'll know what we have to do.

"Hopefully we can push hard to bring it home again."

With so few points separating the top three, it's worth reminding everyone how points are earned in the County Championship.

There are a maximum of 48 points available in the final two matches, but Somerset could win the last two games and still not finish top, given the variations in bonus points.

Fans will be out with their calculators during the four days as they work out the permutations for the teams involved.

Batting bonus points (for runs scored in first 110 overs of first innings):

Bowling bonus points (for wickets taken in first 110 overs of first innings):

Therefore a team can accrue up to eight bonus points to go with the points for winning, drawing and losing, with the possibility of a full 24 points on offer for a win.

While Somerset and Nottinghamshire chase historical, landmark successes, Warwickshire have no such burden.

If the other two are Roger Federer and Rafa Nadal, the Bears are the Novak Djokovic, coming up quietly on the rails to potentially spoil the party.

Ex-England bowler Chris Woakes led them to a thrilling one-wicket triumph over Sussex last month and they have dominated their past two matches, winning both by an innings as they go in search of a ninth Championship and first since the three-conference Covid season of 2021.

The Edgbaston side needed little more than 150 overs to take those 40 wickets, with their seam attack, led by Ethan Bamber, firing on all cylinders, a fact acknowledged by captain Ed Barnard.

"It was nice to get some rewards, I think I've bowled well all year and we've got a great attack with a great spinner, we're in a fortunate place at the moment," he said.

"It feels really exciting. We're trying not to think about it too much and obviously there are two massive games to go."

With so much at stake, the BBC will be right across the remaining two rounds of the County Championship.

Radio: There will be live online commentary of all nine matches in Divisions One and Two from BBC local radio, with matches also featured on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra, Sports Extra 2 and Sports Extra 3, starting on Tuesday.

Online: Our dedicated live text service will be on hand to bring you all the key moments from the deciding weeks of the season. We go live at 10:00 BST on each morning of play.

articles.title: Brendon McCullum wants Kevin Pietersen to challenge methods in England role
articles.summary: Former batter Kevin Pietersen accused England players of not trying on last year's tour of India.
articles.body:
England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum says he wants newly appointed mentor Kevin Pietersen to challenge his methods.

Pietersen criticised England players during the tour of India last year, saying none could say they "did everything they can to try and help England win".

Former batter Pietersen has joined the limited-overs set-up as a specialist mentor until next autumn's 50-over World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

"That [Pietersen's comments] was one of the first things we talked about," McCullum told BBC Sport.

"He said 'gee, I was just criticising you not long ago'.

"I said I don't care about that. Some of it's fair and some of it would need some explanation, but I have no problem with that.

"It's healthy when you create an environment where you're able to challenge.

"That's one thing I want him to do. It's not just bury himself in the batting per se, but look across the entire environment, look across how we run things and what we do, and if there's anything you pick up then just come and challenge me on it.

"Him and I get on well. We had natural respect playing against each other and we spent a bit of time together in the last little while, and I'm super excited to have him as part of our support staff as well."

Pietersen joined up with the squad on Sunday before the first of three T20s and three ODIs against Sri Lanka in Southampton on Tuesday.

Follow ball-by-ball commentary on BBC Sounds, BBC Radio 5 Sports and the BBC Sport website and app. Live text updates and in-play video clips on the website and app. Extended highlights on BBC Two and BBC iPlayer from 23:05 BST.

McCullum said Pietersen was "shocked" when he first called him about "helping us challenge for a World Cup".

The pair had conversations to reach an agreement and McCullum said Pietersen was "unbelievably enthusiastic" about the prospect.

"The energy he's brought to the group already has been immense and you know I feel very privileged for us to be able to have him as a resource within our dressing room," said McCullum.

"He was obviously a brilliant cricketer. He viewed the game quite differently. He was a winner and he was a guy who left no stone unturned when it came to his preparation.

"A lot of these guys grew up watching Kev play and idolised him.

"As a coach, you're trying to provide these guys with the best environment so that they can try and achieve what they want. Adding Kev is certainly that."

England will hand a debut to Derbyshire opener Aneurin Donald in the first T20, with Phil Salt missing through injury.

Donald, who was born in Wales, has impressed in the T20 Blast and The Hundred with Trent Rockets this year and has the highest strike-rate - 232 - of any batter to have faced at least 50 balls in T20s this year.

Pace bowler Jofra Archer is rested after playing all three Tests against Pakistan, but Josh Tongue is included.

England team to face Sri Lanka in first T20: Aneurin Donald, Jos Buttler, Harry Brook (capt), Tom Banton, Jordan Cox, Will Jacks, Jamie Overton, Liam Dawson, Josh Tongue, Sonny Baker, Adil Rashid.

McCullum's sole responsibility is now for the white-ball side after he was sacked as Test coach following the series defeat by New Zealand in June.

England have appointed fellow New Zealander Stephen Fleming to the role.

The pair must juggle the workloads of England's players as they bid to regain the Ashes from Australia next summer before the World Cup.

"We've already been chatting around how we're going to try and manage some of the workloads of players and make sure we still get our best players available for the big series," said McCullum.

"We'll sit down in the coming days and map out a bit of a pathway for a few guys, but naturally guys can't play all year round.

"You're going to have to work out times that you can take them out of the physical duties of international cricket, freshen up, and then other times that you have them all ready to go.

"They will be easy conversations between two good mates with the motivation of what's right for English cricket."

The end of McCullum's reign as Test coach was tainted by off-field issues in Australia during the Ashes, while captain Ben Stokes and seamer Gus Atkinson missed the second Test against New Zealand in June after an incident in a London nightclub.

Since McCullum's departure seamer Brydon Carse has been involved in a nightclub incident while celebrating a victory for Durham.

Test captain Joe Root said he was "hacked off" and had had a "very strong discussion" in the changing room.

McCullum said he is in "total agreement" with Root and that he wants his white-ball side to be the "fittest, strongest, most dynamic, most robust cricket team in the world".

"There is a lot of talent which sits within English cricket and if people aren't prepared to make those sacrifices and to commit to what you're trying to achieve on the field, then other guys will be given those opportunities," said McCullum.

"It's important for Carsey now to just get his house in order and then work his way back towards banging down the door to play for England, because he's still got a long runway in front of him in terms of his career."

articles.title: 'I don’t even know if I’ll be there': ICC Test No.2 Steve Smith uncertain over Ashes 2027 in England
articles.summary: Cricket News: Steve Smith has admitted he is not certain whether he will still be playing Test cricket when Australia travel to England for the 2027 Ashes, raising .
articles.body: Steve Smith has admitted he is not certain whether he will still be playing Test cricket when Australia travel to England for the 2027 Ashes, raising fresh questions over the future of one of Australia's greatest modern batters.The 37-year-old is taking his Test career series by series and has refused to set a retirement date. While the prospect of finally winning an Ashes series in England remains an attraction, Smith acknowledged that he could walk away from Test cricket before next summer's series.“I don’t even know if I’ll be there yet,” Smith told The Telegraph when asked about the 2027 Ashes.Smith keeps retirement decision openSmith has made it clear that he is not thinking too far ahead with his Test career. Instead, the Australian batter is assessing his motivation and energy after each series.“I’m kind of a series-by-series proposition, as I’ve been for a while,” he said.Smith has already enjoyed an extraordinary Test career, featuring in 125 Tests and scoring 37 centuries. He is also currently ranked second among men's Test batters, behind England's Harry Brook. Despite his age, Smith said he is still enjoying playing cricket and has no fixed retirement date.“I’ve achieved a lot in the game. It’s been a great ride for the last 15 years or thereabouts. I’ve had a lot of fun. I’m still enjoying it, so I don’t have an end date, we’ll wait and see,” he said.Winning an Ashes series in England still on his listOne of the few major achievements missing from Smith's illustrious career is winning an Ashes series outright in England. Australia retained the Ashes during Smith's tours in 2019 and 2023, with both series ending 2-2. However, Australia have not won an Ashes series in England since 2001.Smith admitted that winning the Ashes in England would be special, but the possibility of achieving that goal is not enough for him to commit to playing in 2027.“I’d love to win one there or to have won one there, but you wait and see if that comes to fruition,” he said.Smith turns his attention to LA 2028 OlympicsRather than making the 2027 Ashes his main long-term target, Smith revealed that his biggest ambition at this stage of his career is to represent Australia at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Cricket will return to the Olympic programme at LA 2028 in the T20 format, giving Smith another reason to continue developing his game in the shortest format.The Australian is currently playing for the Amsterdam Flames in the European T20 Premier League, with Smith saying that one of his motivations for joining the competition was to play more T20 cricket.“Right now probably it’s just the Olympics to try to be a part of that,” Smith said.Australia will travel to South Africa for a three-game Test series in October, which is Smith’s first Test trip to the country since the 2018 ball-tampering scandal that led to his 12-month ban from international cricket.“Oh, for me, it’s just another series. All that happened a long time ago, and we’ve played a lot of cricket – we’ve been back to South Africa since then for one-dayers. They’re a good side at the moment – obviously beat us in the World Test Championship final. They have a really good pace attack as well, so should be a cracker of a series.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: England coach Brendon McCullum wants Kevin Pietersen to 'challenge' him, has 'no problem' with previous criticisms
articles.summary: Brendon McCullum hopes Kevin Pietersen's "big personality" and "fierce competitiveness" can help England become best white-ball team in the world; KP now a mentor as side build for 2027 50-over World Cup; watch first T20 vs Sri Lanka live on Sky Sports from 6pm Tuesday (6.30pm first ball)
articles.body:
Pietersen will work with England for most series up to and including the 2027 World Cup, starting during the three T20s and as many ODIs at home to Sri Lanka this month.

The 46-year-old, who scored almost 14,000 runs across all three formats of international cricket between 2004 and 20144, accused England of a lack of preparation during a white-ball tour of India in 2025 in which they lost ODI and T20I series.

Speaking ahead of Tuesday's opening T20 in Southampton - live on Sky Sports from 6pm (6.30pm first ball) - McCullum said it was his decision to bring Pietersen onto the coaching staff and hopes his "big personality" will rub off onto the players.

The New Zealander told reporters: "When I rang him and asked whether he would be interested in coming and working with England, I think he thought I was joking for a start!

"He mentioned that he has been quite critical of us in the past and I said, 'I have no problem with that, mate'. There are parts I might agree with and parts I might not agree with and that's fine.

"The way he looks at the game is quite different to a lot of people and if someone can see something different and point that out to help you to become better, then I see that as no bad thing. Kev will do that and I have encouraged him to do that.

"I don't want him to be buried in one specific skillset - I want him to look across the set-up and challenge me privately on ways we can improve and do things differently."

McCullum continued: "The beauty of Kev coming in is that he has an incredible pedigree as a player - a lot of our players grew up watching and idolising him when he was in his pomp as a player.

"He is one of those guys where he has so much in his life so for him to give up those things to focus on trying to help us to get to the level we want and challenge for World Cups, we are incredibly lucky.

"Kev was an unbelievable player and a winner. He left no stone unturned with his preparation. He believed in himself in those big moments and more often than not performed in those moments. He is a big personality and fiercely competitive.

"They are attributes we would love to rub off onto our players. It is great to be able to add a resource like that and I only see an upside.

"He has brought a ton of energy to the set-up within the last 24 hours. His work ethic is second to none and when he is in on something, he is all in.

"I am super excited to have him, he is excited and the boys are buzzing."

Asked whether he had not been questioned enough by his other coaches, McCullum, 44, said: "That is the perception but the reality is that we are always challenging each other.

"I just wanted to add someone of Kev's stature as we look to become one of the best teams in T20 and one-day international cricket."

McCullum would not be drawn on whether success in this role could lead to Pietersen working with the Test team, saying reporters would have to ask incoming red-ball coach Stephen Fleming.

McCullum: We want our best players available across formats

Fleming replaced McCullum as England Test boss in August but did not oversee the 3-0 sweep of Pakistan, with Marcus Trescothick in interim charge for that resounding victory.

Fleming's first official assignment will be the three-Test series in South Africa over the Christmas period, although he has arrived in England from his native New Zealand for a flying visit that will include meeting Test captain Joe Root and chatting with the counties.

The former Chennai Super Kings head coach will link up with McCullum for the third and final T20 against Sri Lanka at Emirates Old Trafford at the weekend, where a big topic of discussion will be how the duo manage England's multi-format stars moving forward.

The 2027 50-over World Cup will take place a few months after the side aim to win an Ashes series for the first time in over a decade, with Harry Brook, Joe Root, Jofra Archer and Jacob Bethell among those set to be key in both tournaments.

McCullum added: "We have a big schedule with an Ashes and World Cup to aim for down the line but also big series coming up.

"We want to make sure we have access as often as possible to the best players across the formats and be aware of workloads as well. There is a bit to pick over but we will get there.

"The timing is perfect [for Fleming to be Test coach] and the team will respond to his style and his approach. He is a brilliant man, coach and tactician.

"He will do a brilliant job and I look forward to working collaboratively with him across the formats and getting the best for all three forms."

McCullum also confirmed that talks will be held over where assistant coach Trescothick now fits into the set-up.

articles.title: 'I’ll definitely come back': Kuldeep Yadav promises Yorkshire return after stunning 10-wicket haul
articles.summary: Cricket News: Kuldeep Yadav’s short stint with Yorkshire has already produced a performance that neither the player nor the county will forget anytime soon. The Ind.
articles.body: Kuldeep Yadav’s short stint with Yorkshire has already produced a performance that neither the player nor the county will forget anytime soon. The India left-arm wrist-spinner claimed his first 10-wicket haul in first-class cricket as Yorkshire crushed Essex by an innings and 106 runs at Headingley, securing their Division One status with three days to spare.Kuldeep finished with match figures of 10-120, taking 4-70 in Essex’s first innings before returning to claim 6-50 in the second. His performance earned him the County Championship Player of the Round award and underlined his ability to influence matches with the red ball.The spell was particularly impressive because Headingley is not traditionally regarded as a spin-dominated venue. Kuldeep said he initially found little assistance from the surface but focused on making the batters create their own mistakes.“It wasn’t a rank turner; Headingley is not known for that,” Kuldeep said in a statement on Monday “I was just trying to make the batters make mistakes.”His approach changed in the second innings when he spotted an opportunity to exploit the footmarks outside the stumps. By changing his angles and bowling both over and around the wicket, he repeatedly troubled Essex’s middle order.Yorkshire already want him backThe performance has also strengthened Kuldeep’s relationship with Yorkshire, who signed him on a short-term deal in July. His spell with the county was interrupted by his involvement with India during their Test series in Sri Lanka, while he also featured in Yorkshire’s defeat against Surrey at The Oval.Despite the interruptions, Kuldeep has made a strong impression inside the Yorkshire dressing room. He has now promised to return to the County Championship, describing Headingley as his “ultimate home” after completing his first 10-wicket match haul.“When I was about to get the sixth one, I thought, ‘Give me one more, let me complete the ten-wicket haul!’” he said.“I’ll definitely come back, that’s a promise.”Yorkshire head coach Anthony McGrath made it clear that the county would welcome another stint from the spinner. He praised Kuldeep’s control and his ability to constantly change angles and set batters up.“You could see how much he spins it and his control of spin was just sensational,” McGrath said.The spinner has also quickly built a strong relationship with Yorkshire’s other players. Off-spinner Dom Bess, who took five wickets in the match and shared an 83-run eighth-wicket partnership with Kuldeep in the first innings, highlighted the Indian’s enthusiasm for the craft.“The thing I love about KD is the love of craft. He comes here to play and absolutely loves it,” Bess said.McGrath believes Yorkshire would have little hesitation in bringing Kuldeep back, saying the county would “bite his hand off” to sign him for another campaign.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Are they living in the past?': Ex-India cricketer slams Mohsin Naqvi after Asia Cup trophy snub
articles.summary: Cricket News: India's Women's Asia Cup triumph in Dubai was overshadowed by another awkward trophy presentation involving Asian Cricket Council president Mohsin Naq.
articles.body: India's Women's Asia Cup triumph in Dubai was overshadowed by another awkward trophy presentation involving Asian Cricket Council president Mohsin Naqvi, as the champions once again declined to collect the silverware from the Pakistan Cricket Board chief.India defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final on Sunday to claim the title, but the post-match ceremony was held up amid the standoff. Naqvi, who is also Pakistan's Interior Minister, remained at the venue, but India's players were unwilling to receive the trophy from him.The episode was strikingly similar to last year's men's Asia Cup final, when India's victorious team had also refused to accept the trophy from Naqvi. The repeat has once again put the spotlight on his dual role as a senior cricket administrator and a prominent figure in Pakistan's government.Mohammad Kaif questions Naqvi's dual responsibilitiesFormer India batter Mohammad Kaif has questioned whether Naqvi can give sufficient attention to cricket administration while simultaneously handling major political responsibilities.“Are they living in the past? Don't they have a reality check? Mohsin Naqvi is in politics. He is the boss of the board. It's not like that,” Kaif said on Cricbuzz.“If you are in cricket, then you have to be in cricket. You have to go to two places. It's a difficult job. You won't be able to give time. You have so many political commitments. You have to run the cricket board. You have to see what's going on inside. You have to stop at one place and invest time. If you look at any body, if you compare it with the BCCI, or look at it from the outside, nobody does two things.”Naqvi's responsibilities extend beyond the PCB. As ACC president, PCB chairman and Pakistan's Interior Minister, he occupies influential positions across both cricket and government, making his involvement in major India-Pakistan cricket events particularly sensitive.Kaif believes leading a cricket board demands a level of focus that can be difficult to provide while holding another major office.“Either you are a politician, or you are a cricketer. You have to balance it. You have to focus on one thing,” he said.Kaif also rejected the idea that Pakistan's cricketing problems stem from a lack of talented players.According to the former India international, Pakistan continues to possess considerable natural ability but needs a better system and the right people to turn that talent into successful professional cricketers.“Players aren't bad. You need people who make players. There is a lot of talent in Pakistan,” he added.The latest controversy has ensured that India's Women's Asia Cup victory will be remembered for more than the 72-run win over Sri Lanka. Instead of a routine trophy celebration, the final once again ended with an unresolved presentation involving Naqvi.With a similar situation having played out at the men's Asia Cup final last year, questions over Naqvi's role at the intersection of cricket administration and politics are likely to remain part of the conversation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mohsin Naqvi 'didn't object' to India refusing Women's Asia Cup trophy from him, says Rajeev Shukla
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla on Monday said the Indian women's team's decision not to receive the Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket C.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla on Monday said the Indian women's team's decision not to receive the Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) chairman Mohsin Naqvi was taken collectively by the Board, adding that Naqvi "did not raise any objection" to it.India beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Asia Cup final in Dubai on Sunday, but the team did not accept the trophy from Naqvi. It was the second year in a row that an Indian team skipped receiving the Asia Cup trophy from the ACC chairman, after the men's team did the same during the 2025 Asia Cup following the Pahalgam terror attack.“We discussed the matter among ourselves and decided that we would not accept it (trophy) from him. It was our collective decision. He (Naqvi) also did not raise any objection to it,” Shukla told reporters after arriving with the team at the Indira Gandhi International Airport.“We informed our team accordingly, and he presented it to whoever he had to and then left,” Shukla added, as quoted by news agency PTI.Shukla's comments were in line with BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia's explanation after the final.Saikia had said the Board's stand changed after the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, while adding that India would continue to play Pakistan in multinational tournaments in line with the government's policy.“Our men’s team won the Asia Cup a year and a half ago. And our whole situation, since the April 2025 Pahalgam incident, changed after that. So, after that, there was pressure on us from our citizens that we shouldn’t keep any relations with our neighboring country and not play cricket with them. But our government has a policy that we must play against every country in multinational tournaments,” Saikia had told IANS.“But that doesn’t mean we will follow every condition laid out for us. Our military conflict is still ongoing. One of the main leaders who is working against the interests of our country; we can’t receive the trophy from him. The Women’s team has expressed solidarity with the decision taken by the men’s team last year,” Saikia had said.Earlier, pictures had surfaced showing Saikia talking to Naqvi during the Asia Cup final in Dubai. Responding to the criticism over those images, Shukla said it was only a professional interaction during the match.“What Saikia ji said is absolutely correct. When you are at a match, everyone is present there and interacts in a professional capacity. Therefore, I do not think there should be so much criticism over that,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘You don’t treat human beings that way’: Michael Holding slams Pakistan over Imran Khan’s treatment
articles.summary: Cricket News: Former West Indies pacer Michael Holding has joined the growing list of cricketing figures calling for better treatment of former Pakistan captain Imr.
articles.body: Former West Indies pacer Michael Holding has joined the growing list of cricketing figures calling for better treatment of former Pakistan captain Imran Khan, saying the imprisoned 1992 World Cup winner should be treated “just like another human being”.Imran has been in a Pakistani prison since 2023 while facing ongoing legal cases, with concerns over his health and access to basic facilities continuing to grow. His family has claimed that he does not even have access to books and has not been provided proper medical facilities.The issue gained fresh attention after 21 international captains including Sunil Gavaskar and Kapil Dev, wrote to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, urging authorities to ensure basic amenities for Imran. Pat Cummins, Wasim Akram, Javed Miandad and Brian Lara also subsequently spoke in support of humane treatment for the former Pakistan all-rounder.Michael Holding speaks out for Imran KhanHolding, who played alongside and against Imran during their international careers, said the situation involving the former Pakistan captain was deeply upsetting.“I'll mention one name, Imran Khan, but you probably don't want to go down the political route, and I don't want to either, but that's a sad story. become one of the former Pakistan captain’s defining legacies. I played with Imran, I wouldn't say I played a lot. I played some one-day games with him. I played county cricket, a few games against Imran, but apart from playing with Imran, I have spent time with Imran,” Holding told Sports Now.The former fast bowler recalled his association with Imran away from cricket as well. He remembered accompanying him in London when the former Pakistan captain was raising funds for his cancer hospital."When Imran was going around London looking to garner funds for that cancer hospital, I went around with him, I tried to support him as best as I possibly could, where that was concerned. So I know the man, and I know exactly what type of person that he is. And it's extremely sad to see the situation now and what is going on with Imran Khan," the 72-year-old recalled.Holding's comments came after the appeal from former international captains seeking proper medical care and family access for Imran. The West Indies great backed that demand while stressing that the issue should not be viewed simply through the prism of politics.'You don't treat human beings that way'Holding said he fully supported the captains who had written to the Pakistan Prime Minister and questioned why Imran should be treated differently from other prisoners."I am in total support of the captains who wrote that letter. I don't know what effect it will have, but I am in total support of trying to get the man to be treated just like another human being. You don't treat human beings that way. People who have committed murder aren't treated that way. So I don't see the reason why this man should be treated that way," Holding said.He also questioned whether jealousy could be a factor, pointing to Imran's extraordinary global profile.“I don't know if there's jealousy involved in this, because Imran Khan. I don't think there's a Pakistani that is more well known around the world than Imran Khan. That is ridiculous, the way the man is being treated,” he added.The controversy surrounding Imran's prison conditions had already spilled into the cricketing world after Michael Atherton interviewed his sons, Sulaiman and Kasim, on the sidelines of the Lord's Test between England and Pakistan. The PCB subsequently threatened to pull out of the fixture, but Sky Sports went ahead and broadcast the 18-minute interview.In the interview, Imran's sons alleged that their father was being denied proper medical facilities. Holding's intervention has now added another prominent voice to the calls for humane treatment of the former Pakistan captain.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Kris Srikkanth has questioned India’s decision to leave Vaibhav Sooryavanshi out of the playing XI for the opening T20I against Afghanistan, with the former India captain and chief selector alleging that the teenage batter is not being treated fairly.The selection call came amid a familiar opening dilemma for India following Sanju Samson’s return to the squad. The team management ultimately opted for Samson and Abhishek Sharma at the top, leaving Sooryavanshi on the bench.Srikkanth questions Sooryavanshi’s exclusionThe decision was particularly surprising given Sooryavanshi’s impact in India’s previous T20I assignment. The 15-year-old was named Player of the Series against Zimbabwe after scoring 151 runs at a stunning strike rate of 196.10.Sooryavanshi had also only recently featured in the Duleep Trophy final, meaning he had very little time to make the transition from red-ball cricket back to T20 cricket.Srikkanth admitted he was surprised by the call and revealed that even his wife questioned why the youngster was not playing.“Yesterday, because Sooryavanshi didn’t play, we started watching a movie. My wife was shouting that Sooryavanshi didn’t play and started arguing that someone who was the Player of the Match in the last match isn’t playing. Even my wife is questioning his exclusion. You are not treating Sooryavanshi properly. Now, if he plays the next match, he’ll wonder whether he’ll be dropped if he doesn’t score," Srikkanth said on his YouTube channel.The former selector believes India need to show greater faith in Sooryavanshi, especially after the teenager’s performances in domestic cricket and the IPL for Rajasthan Royals.He also cautioned that frequent changes at the top could create uncertainty for the batters involved, with players unsure about how secure their places are.‘I pity Samson’Srikkanth also took aim at the way Samson has been managed by the Indian team.Samson was part of India’s starting combination at the beginning of their UK campaign in July but was replaced by Sooryavanshi after three matches. He returned for the seventh and final game of the tour before being rested for the subsequent Zimbabwe series.According to Srikkanth, neither Samson nor Sooryavanshi is benefiting from being given sporadic opportunities. He urged the management to settle on a clearer approach instead of rotating the two players in and out of the side.“This team management is playing around with Sanju Samson. I pity Samson. Either you give him an extended run and then drop him or give Vaibhav Sooryavanshi a run of matches without dropping him. The mistake India are making is both are getting two matches here and there. That’s not good for the player," Srikkanth said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Will get both our trophies back,' asserts BCCI after not accepting silverware from ACC chief Mohsin Naqvi
articles.summary: Cricket News: MUMBAI: A familiar script has repeated itself. And ironically, at the same venue - the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. Almost 12 months after Sur.
articles.body: MUMBAI: A familiar script has repeated itself. And ironically, at the same venue - the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. Almost 12 months after Suryakumar Yadav's victorious Indian team came home without the Asia Cup Trophy, refusing to accept it from Mohsin Naqvi, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman, who is currently heading the Asian Cricket Council (ACC) and Pakistan's interior minister, Harmanpreet Kaur & Co did an encore after clinching the 2026 Women's Asia Cup in Dubai, shunning the trophy ceremony on Sunday night due to the presence of Naqvi on the stage.Like in case of the men's team, the women's team too returned home empty - despite triumphing in the Asia Cup women's championship in style, winning all their five matches, including recording a thumping 72-run win over Sri Lanka in a one-sided final on Sunday.Naqvi showed up at the stadium minutes before the last ball was bowled and insisted on presenting the winners' trophy himself, despite being told by the BCCI authorities clearly that the Indian women's team would not accept the trophy from him. It was a repeat show of what the Indian men's team did on September 28 last year. The brief and delayed presentation ceremony eventually concluded without the winners receiving their prize.There were behind-the-scenes discussions over the post-match formalities, with the BCCI proposing that ACC vice-president Khalid Al Zarooni could present the trophy. However, Naqvi did not relent. He stood on the podium and handed the runners-up cheque to the Sri Lankan team. Al Zarooni, Sri Lanka Cricket Transformation Committee head Eran Wickramaratne, Emirates Cricket Board (ECB) secretary general Mubashir Usmani and a female representative of DP World, the title sponsor of the Asia Cup, were among those on the podium.BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia and vice-president Rajeev Shukla were present in the stadium but they did not go up on the dais or share the stage with Naqvi. There were visuals of Saikia and Shukla speaking cordially with Naqvi in the Royal Box that went viral. They spoke to Team Indian on the ground, presented them medals and congratulated them on their record-extending eighth Asia Cup title. "At some point, we would get both our Asia Cup trophies back," Saikia asserted, while talking to TOI from Dubai.Explaining India's uncompromising stand regarding not receiving the trophy from Naqvi, Saikia told this paper, "We had taken a conscious decision considering all prevailing aspects, and our position had been communicated to the ACC in advance, that the Indian team would not participate in the trophy presentation under the circumstances.Our participation in the Asia Cup was in fulfilment of our sporting commitments as a member of the Asian Cricket Council by adhering to the policy in place, and there was never any question of compromising on the spirit of the game or our commitment to international cricket.However, participation in a multinational tournament and the manner in which the trophy is presented or received are two separate and distinct issues.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs AFG: Nitish Reddy in focus as India look to fill in allrounders' slot
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: There's growing concern in Indian cricket over the paucity of seam-bowling allrounders. The team management and the selectors are forever i.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: There's growing concern in Indian cricket over the paucity of seam-bowling allrounders. The team management and the selectors are forever in the hunt to find a backup for the injury-prone Hardik Pandya. Even India's dominant win over Afghanistan in the first T20I here on Sunday night couldn't mask the big crack in their armour.Nitish Kumar Reddy and Shivam Dube went for 51 runs in the three overs they bowled. More than the runs conceded, the fact that they came on to bowl only after the four frontline bowlers had broken the back of the Afghan batting is what will be more disconcerting for the team management. Captain Shreyas Iyer did go to Reddy first to bowl the quota of the fifth bowler, but couldn't throw the ball back to him after two overs.It's understandable that Reddy is also coming back from a three-month injury layoff while Dube has been bowling very little over the last two-three years. But it's an area that the Indian team management is eager to cover when the prep for the ODI World Cup begins after the Asian Games. Effectively, the next T20Is against Afghanistan on Tuesday and Thursday before the Asian Games will be an audition for Reddy.Pandya is still working at the Centre of Excellence (CoE) on his fitness to be available to bowl 10 overs in an ODI. But the selectors are hamstrung by injuries to every potential option. Reddy himself spends as much time at the CoE as Pandya. Now, it has emerged that Suryansh Shedge and Venkatesh Iyer are too nursing injuries. Harshit Rana, too, has been breaking down frequently. It's a bizarre situation for the selectors. Reddy is slated to be in Japan for the Asian Games when India play an ODI series against West Indies at home later this month.There's no clarity on when Hardik will be declared fit for an international match. Thus, the next two matches here at the Kotla become extremely crucial for both Reddy and Dube.Varun ruled out of Afghanistan series, fresh blow to CoEVarun Chakravarthy has been ruled out of the rest of two T20Is against Afghanistan to be played on Tuesday and Thursday. The details of the injury are awaited.His participation in the upcoming Asian Games will be decided after the BCCI's medical team assesses the injury. Chakravarthy's injury is another jolt to the BCCI's Centre of Excellence (CoE) under cricket head VVS Laxman.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
